summary.posture: The hardening work on this branch is present and verifiable in source: install lock auto-creation in both container entrypoints, installer input validation and LOCK_EX writes, non-guessable seeded admin hash, admin login rate limiting plus forced default-password rotation, uploads/storage PHP-execution denial and dotfile denial in both nginx configurations, security headers, empty-by-default TRUSTED_PROXIES, CSRF exemptions limited to pay notify/return, payment credentials encrypted at rest via an APP_KEY-backed cast and masked in the admin UI, and fail-closed notify handlers in the epay controller. Residual configuration risk concentrates in (1) the installer staying anonymously reachable whenever install.lock is absent while POST /do-install overwrites .env and executes a 21-DROP install.sql, and (2) database/sql/install.sql shipping 29 payment rows whose signing secrets are literal documentation placeholders, 26 of them is_open=1, so a fresh install exposes forgeable notify endpoints until an operator rotates keys.
summary.session_cookie_state: http_only=true, same_site=lax, secure=false in .env.example (config default null => false), encrypt=false, lifetime 120 minutes, expire_on_close=false, remember-me enabled on the admin guard; container PHP also has session.use_strict_mode=Off and session.cookie_secure=Off.
summary.install_lock_state: Lock is created automatically only by the container entrypoints (Dockerfile:11-17, conf/start.sh:28-30) when INSTALL != true. The manual (non-Docker) deployment guide in debian_manual.md never creates it. The lock is a pure file-existence check (app/Http/Middleware/InstallCheck.php:19-23) with no content, ownership or age validation, and it is written only after .env rewrite + install.sql import + admin row update.

install_lock.gate: app/Http/Middleware/InstallCheck.php:19-23 - redirects to '/' when base_path()/install.lock exists, otherwise forwards the request.
install_lock.boot_gate: app/Http/Middleware/DujiaoBoot.php:20-23 - every dujiaoka.boot route is redirected to /install while the lock file is absent.
install_lock.routes: routes/common/web.php:37-42 - GET /install and POST /do-install are the only routes in the install.check group; both inherit the 'web' group (routes/web.php:14-21, app/Providers/RouteServiceProvider.php:61-63), so CSRF applies but no authentication does.

install_lock.lock_creation_container_arm64: conf/start.sh:28-30 (copied by Dockerfile-ARM64:25) - same INSTALL gate, executed before `php artisan clear-compiled` (conf/start.sh:34).

findings.title: Installer is anonymously reachable whenever install.lock is missing, and do-install rewrites .env plus runs a 21-DROP schema

evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: HomeController.php:184-202 builds .env from .env.example and file_put_contents($envPath,...); :204 DB::unprepared(file_get_contents(install.sql)); :206-211 rewrites admin_users id=1 with attacker-supplied username/password; :216 writes the lock only afterwards
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: database/sql/install.sql:7,54,72,102,120,138,157,178,190,206,228,252,275,299,316,343,365,401,422,443,483 - all application tables dropped; .env (DB, Redis, APP_KEY, ADMIN_ROUTE_PREFIX) replaced
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: Lock creation happens only in containers (Dockerfile:14, conf/start.sh:28-30) and requires INSTALL != true; the manual deployment path in debian_manual.md never creates it

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: Both container entrypoints auto-create the lock when INSTALL=false (the default), the POST needs a valid CSRF token, and docs/php83-upgrade-deployment.md:153-156 tells operators to pre-create install.lock. The exposure therefore requires a deployment where the lock was never created (manual/LEMP per debian_manual.md, a container started with INSTALL=true and no lock volume, or a deleted lock) - but in that state the control is a single file-existence check with no auth in front of a destructive installer.
preconditions: install.lock absent
installer reachable over the network
CSRF token obtained from GET /install

findings.title: install.sql enables 26 payment gateways whose signing secrets are literal documentation placeholders

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: database/sql/install.sql:506-535 pays seed rows; database/sql/install.sql:515 (yipay alipay is_open=2), :516 (yipay wxpay, key '密钥', is_open=1), :519-520 (vpay, key placeholder, is_open=1), :521 (stripe, 'sk开头的密钥'), :525-534 (tokenpay, '你的API密钥', is_open=1)
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Service/PayService.php:28-35 selects where('is_open', STATUS_OPEN) and app/Service/PayService.php:47-54 detailByCheck does the same, so is_open=1 rows are live
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/VpayController.php:71-84, MapayController.php:71-81, PaysapiController.php:98-108, TokenPayController.php:71-97 - callback signature = md5/hmac over request fields + the stored key, so a published key makes forged 'payment succeeded' callbacks verifiable
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: database/sql/upgrade-php83.sql:65-66 (UPDATE pays SET is_open=0; then =1 only for /pay/yipay) shows the intended default, but a fresh install.sql import never gets it

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: The values are advisory placeholders that an operator is expected to replace, the attacker still needs a valid order_sn (visible to whoever created the order) and completedOrder re-checks the amount against actual_price (which the attacker supplies in the forged callback, so that check does not block it). Epusdt/Coinbase seed rows are is_open=0 and the upgrade script disables everything except yipay, which narrows but does not remove the risk because the enabled yipay rows also keep the literal key '密钥' until rotated.
preconditions: fresh install.sql import (or upgrade without rotating keys)
gateway left is_open=1 with placeholder secret
attacker knows or can create the target order_sn

findings.title: Session cookies lack the Secure flag by default and PHP runs without session.use_strict_mode

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: .env.example:69 SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=false; config/session.php:169 secure => env('SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE', null); config/session.php:49 encrypt=false; :182 http_only=true; :197 same_site='lax'
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: conf/php.ini:8 sets only session.cookie_httponly; `php -i` in dujiaoka:2.1.0-php83 reports session.cookie_secure=Off and session.use_strict_mode=Off
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: admin guard sessions (config/admin.php:130-162) and every front-end order page share the same cookie policy; config/admin.php:152 remember=true issues a long-lived remember cookie
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: README.md:34 and debian_manual.md tell operators to set SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true, i.e. the secure default is opt-in

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: The cookie is encrypted (EncryptCookies has no exceptions), HttpOnly is on, SameSite=Lax blocks most cross-site CSRF-style leakage, and dcat regenerates the session id on login (vendor AuthController.php:239); the residual risk is plaintext transport of a privileged cookie on http deployments and fixation of never-seen ids.
preconditions: deployment served over plain HTTP or mixed content
operator does not set SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE=true

findings.title: HSTS / https-aware behaviour silently disabled behind a TLS-terminating proxy because TRUSTED_PROXIES defaults to empty

evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Http/Middleware/TrustProxies.php:19,28-35 - $proxies remains null unless a non-empty string is supplied
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: app/Http/Middleware/SecurityHeaders.php:20-22 adds Strict-Transport-Security only when $request->isSecure(); ADMIN_HTTPS defaults to false (.env.example:47-49, config/admin.php:117)
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: No HSTS in conf/default.conf or conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf (headers are X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy only)

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: Direct TLS termination inside nginx (as in debian_manual.md) makes isSecure() true and HSTS is emitted; the issue only appears in the common reverse-proxy topology where the operator leaves TRUSTED_PROXIES empty, which also degrades the login rate limiter key to the proxy IP.
preconditions: TLS terminated by an upstream proxy
TRUSTED_PROXIES left empty

findings.title: SMTP password and push/bot tokens are cached in plaintext under a single Redis key with no TTL

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: app/Admin/Forms/SystemSetting.php:20 Cache::put('system-setting', $input); fields at :64 telegram_bot_token, :71 bark_token, :74 qywxbot_key, :81 password (SMTP), :88 geetest_key
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Helpers/functions.php:58-62 reads the cache on every request; config/mail.php:18-19 documents that SMTP settings come from this cache
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: app/Service/MailConfigService.php:23-35 applies host/username/password to the mailer; app/Admin/Forms/SystemSetting.php:99 returns the same array to the admin form
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: .env.example:31 CACHE_DRIVER=redis; config/cache.php:21 default store; the payment secrets get an encrypted cast (app/Models/Pay.php:15-19) but system settings get none

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: Writing requires an authenticated admin, the cache lives in Redis rather than the database, and Redis is normally reachable only from the app network; this is an at-rest/defence-in-depth gap (any Redis snapshot, backup, monitor command or weak Redis password exposes mail credentials) rather than a directly reachable vulnerability.
preconditions: admin access to the system-setting form to seed the value
read access to the Redis instance or its backups

findings.title: Primary Dockerfile runs the queue worker unsupervised, and a queue failure inside the post-commit dispatch block turns a successful payment into 'fail'

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: Dockerfile:15 - `su application -s /bin/sh -c "php artisan queue:work --tries=3" >/tmp/work.log 2>&1 &` inside the generated start.sh; conf/start.sh:36 `exec supervisord`; conf/supervisord.conf:30-41 only exists in the ARM64 image
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:392-457 - DB::commit() at line 435 followed by ServerJiang/Telegram/Bark/WorkWeiXin/ApiHook dispatches at 437-452 inside the try whose catch at 454 throws RuleValidationException
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/*.php notify handlers translate that exception into a gateway-visible failure (YipayController.php:100-108 guarded; EpusdtController.php:94, TokenPayController.php:95, VpayController.php:84, PaysapiController.php:107, MapayController.php:80 unguarded and would surface as HTTP 500)
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: .env.example:36 QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis makes Redis a hard dependency of the payment acknowledgement path; config/queue.php:61-67 retry_after 90 / block_for null

findings.code:
// Dockerfile:14-16
'if [ "$INSTALL" != "true" ] && [ ! -e /app/install.lock ]; then echo ok > /app/install.lock; fi' 
'su application -s /bin/sh -c "php artisan queue:work --tries=3" >/tmp/work.log 2>&1 &' 
'exec supervisord'
findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: The order is already committed before dispatch, so no payment data is lost; a retried gateway notification hits the idempotent branch in OrderProcessService.php:400-410 (same trade_no acknowledged). The impact is therefore duplicate/failed acknowledgements plus stalled mail/expiry jobs, not direct tampering - and the ARM64 image uses a supervised worker.
preconditions: non-ARM image or manual supervisor setup
queue/Redis unavailability, or the detached worker exits

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy, and security headers are applied to the 'web' group only

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: app/Http/Kernel.php:42 (SecurityHeaders only in 'web'); :45-48 ('api' group has throttle + bindings only)
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: admin and storefront pages get nosniff/frame-options/referrer/permissions; any api-group JSON response gets none
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: conf/default.conf:10-13 and conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf:4-7 also stop at those four headers; no CSP and no HSTS

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: The templates escape output and X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN blocks framing; missing CSP is a defence-in-depth gap, not a standalone exploit, and nginx duplicates the headers for static files.

findings.title: PHP ini hardening gaps in the shipped images (no open_basedir/disable_functions, display_startup_errors On)

evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: `php -i` in dujiaoka:2.1.0-php83: display_startup_errors=On, allow_url_fopen=On, disable_functions=(empty), open_basedir=(unset), opcache.validate_timestamps=On
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: all PHP execution inside the container (web, queue worker, artisan)
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: Positive controls present: expose_php=Off, display_errors=Off, cgi.fix_pathinfo=0, session.cookie_httponly=1, nginx server_tokens off

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: These settings matter only after a code-execution primitive exists; PHP-FPM already runs as the unprivileged 'application' user (conf/fpm-pool.conf:5-6) and the web root is /app/public.
preconditions: an additional RCE/LFI primitive

findings.title: FPM pool passes the container environment to workers and exposes status/ping paths in config (not routed by the shipped vhost)

evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: clear_env=no means every container env var is visible through getenv()/$_ENV in PHP
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: ARM64 image only (Dockerfile-ARM64:22 copies conf/fpm-pool.conf); the webdevops image keeps its own pool file
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: conf/default.conf has no /fpm-status or /fpm-ping location, so requests fall through to the front controller (verified by reading the whole file)

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: Status/ping are unreachable without a matching nginx location or a wider listener, and environment leakage requires an existing info-disclosure primitive.
preconditions: a future nginx/proxy rule that forwards /fpm-status
or an existing env-dump primitive

findings.title: Compose publishes 9000/tcp even though php-fpm binds loopback, and the container masters run as root

evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: config/fpm-pool.conf is not used by the webdevops image; verified there /usr/local/etc/php-fpm.d/application.conf also has listen = 127.0.0.1:9000
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: host port 9000 is bound by the container but nothing listens on non-loopback addresses
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: conf/supervisord.conf:3 user=root, :10 and :21 run php-fpm/nginx masters as root; workers drop to 'application'

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: Because FPM listens on 127.0.0.1 only, the published port is unreachable today; the finding is a latent footgun (and unnecessary attack-surface declaration), not an open FastCGI exposure.
preconditions: a future change to the FPM listen address

findings.title: Mail failure handling leaves misleading config paths and surfaces raw SMTP errors

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: .env.example:51-57 sets MAIL_ENCRYPTION=ssl but config/mail.php:25-35 only reads scheme/host/port/username/password; MAIL_SCHEME is absent from .env.example
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Service/MailConfigService.php:15-16 maps the admin 'encryption' field correctly (ssl->smtps), so the env path and the admin path disagree
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: app/Jobs/MailSend.php:23 (tries=2), :30 (timeout 30), :58-65 (invalid recipient logged with the address), app/Admin/Forms/EmailTest.php:40-45 (raw exception message returned to the admin UI)
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: config/queue.php failed-job database driver + failed_jobs table (install.sql:343-353) records exhausted attempts

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: The exception text is only shown to an authenticated admin, and a failed mail job never blocks payment completion (the dispatch is fire-and-forget). The ignore-MAIL_ENCRYPTION mismatch mainly causes availability/plaintext-transport surprises.
preconditions: SMTP configured through .env only (not the admin form)

findings.title: Stripe charge endpoint returns raw exception text and is a state-changing GET

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: routes/common/pay.php:35-38 (all Stripe endpoints are GET); app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php:21-26 (only pay/*/notify_url and pay/*/return_url are exempt)
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Http/Controllers/Pay/StripeController.php:524-558 - charge() consumes stripeToken/orderid, calls Stripe\Charge::create (:544) and returns $e->getMessage() (:554-556)
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: anonymous storefront; reached via pay-gateway redirect
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: optional order-context HMAC validation at :536 via PayController::validateOrderContextToken (app/Http/Controllers/PayController.php:132-168)

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: CSRF middleware does not protect GET requests in any case, so the exemption list is irrelevant here; charging requires a valid Stripe token, the amount is computed server-side from the order (bcmul at :545), and the order-context token (when present) binds the request to the session-order pair. Error text is Stripe-side detail.
preconditions: stripe gateway enabled

findings.title: Seeded admin password hash is deliberately non-guessable, so the forced-rotation control only covers legacy admin/admin installs

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: database/sql/install.sql:246 (seeded hash, not reproduced here; replaced in commit 71777e0)
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: installs imported directly from install.sql; the installer path is safer because HomeController.php:150-152 enforces a >=10 character password
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: docker read-only check: password_verify('admin', seeded hash) === false

findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: No guessable default credential is shipped, so this is an operational (locked-out admin) rather than a security defect; it is recorded so later phases do not claim a live 'admin/admin' default.

findings.title: install.sql yipay seed uses is_open=2 and leaves the README default-enablement claim inconsistent

evidence.EVID_CFG_CONFIG_LOCATION: database/sql/install.sql:515 - yipay 'alipay' row has is_open=2 (neither STATUS_OPEN=1 nor STATUS_CLOSE=0)
evidence.EVID_CFG_RUNTIME_SETTING: app/Models/BaseModel.php:17-18 defines only 1/0; app/Service/PayService.php:30-33 requires exactly 1
evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: README.md:24 states only yipay is enabled by default; after a fresh import the front end instead offers the other placeholder gateways and hides this yipay row until upgrade-php83.sql:65-66 normalises it
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: The same inconsistency is what keeps CFG-02's placeholder-key gateways live on fresh installs

findings.code:
// database/sql/install.sql:515
INSERT INTO `pays` VALUES (14, '易支付-支付宝', 'alipay', 1, 1, '商户号', '', '密钥', '/pay/yipay', 2, ...);
findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: No security control is bypassed by the stray value; it is a data/expectation mismatch that materially weakens the documented default posture.

findings.title: Local container images predate the working tree entrypoint (install.lock test uses -d instead of -e)

evidence.EVID_CFG_IMPACT_SCOPE: any dynamic verification performed against the prebuilt local images
evidence.EVID_CFG_SECURITY_SWITCH: A directory named install.lock would satisfy -e but not -d, so image behaviour and source behaviour differ

findings.code:
# repo conf/start.sh:28
if [ "$INSTALL" != "true" ] && [ ! -e /app/install.lock ]; then
# image /start.sh:28
if [ "$INSTALL" != "true" ] && [ ! -d /app/install.lock ]; then
findings.why_might_not_be_vulnerable: This is an evidence-quality note, not an application vulnerability; later phases must build fresh images before trusting runtime results.

handoffs.reason: Installer accepts arbitrary DB host/port/credentials and then issues DB::unprepared on install.sql (HomeController.php:160-204); confirm no injection surface into the generated .env values beyond the CRLF whitelist at :138-145.
Installer DB/Redis connection attempts (HomeController.php:168-182) let an anonymous caller make the server connect to arbitrary internal hosts/ports when the lock is absent.

CSRF exemption list is minimal (app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php:21-26), but pay/stripe/charge is a state-changing GET (routes/common/pay.php:35-38) and SameSite=Lax defaults change the cross-site behaviour.

ForceAdminPasswordChange only redirects when session('force_admin_password_change') is set (app/Http/Middleware/ForceAdminPasswordChange.php:41-45); verify no admin route escapes the ['web','admin','admin.force-password'] chain configured in config/admin.php:74.

All supported gateways sign with md5(concatenated fields + secret) (YipayController.php:41/94, VpayController.php:43/79, MapayController.php:45/75, PaysapiController.php:101, TokenPayController.php:67, EpusdtController.php:67) and pays secrets are encrypted with an APP_KEY-backed cast; assess key management and the md5-vs-HMAC choice under the gateway protocols.

notify rejections log order_sn/trade_no (YipayController.php:103-106) and MailSend logs recipient addresses (app/Jobs/MailSend.php:61-63); LOG_LEVEL=warning (.env.example:8) vs hardcoded 'debug' channel levels (config/logging.php:47,53).
StripeController.php:554-556 and app/Admin/Forms/EmailTest.php:40-45 return raw exception messages; APP_DEBUG default is false (.env.example:4) and ignition is require-dev only.

uncertainties: Whether any deployment ships without install.lock cannot be determined statically; the exposure in CFG-01 is conditional on that state.
The plaintext of the seeded admin hash is unknown (password_verify tests for common values returned false) - treated as non-guessable, not as a known default credential.
MAIL_ENCRYPTION-ignored behaviour (CFG-11) was derived from config/mail.php:25-35 (env('MAIL_SCHEME') only); no SMTP connection was attempted in static mode.

Local images dujiaoka:2.1.0-php83 and dujiaoka-php83-arm64-final:latest differ from conf/start.sh (CFG-15); docker-derived runtime facts (php -i, pool listen address, vhost includes) were used only for base-image defaults, not as proof of the current entrypoint logic.

CSRF token acquisition for the installer (needed for CFG-01 exploitation) was inferred from the 'web' middleware group (app/Http/Kernel.php:34-43 + RouteServiceProvider.php:61-63); no HTTP request was sent.
